title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 'Longue Marche' sequel (equation des lacets), Grothendieck studies a group of 'systems' u. Each u acts on the profinite groupoid/group Pi_{0,3}^ (or the tilde version) and is encoded by cocycle-type data f(u), g(u), h(u), alpha(u), beta(u) in Pi^. Their composition laws (10), (11) on the previous page have the form x(u'u) = u'(x(u)) . x(u').

On the previous page these are pushed to a linear quotient SL(2,Z^)' or GL(2,Z^)', presumably the action on the abelianization of Pi or a related quotient. There a group homomorphism phi_sigma replaces the abstract action of u', giving formulas (12) with int(phi_sigma(u')) in place of u'.

This page makes three points.
(i) After linearization the formulas are explicitly computable. In Pi_{0,3}^ itself, an expression like u'(g(u)) cannot be written algebraically from the data f', g', h' that determine u and u'.
(ii) The scalar characters are multiplicative: mu(u'u) = mu(u')mu(u) (13), and hence the sign character epsilon_2(u'u) = epsilon_2(u')epsilon_2(u) (14). Mu is probably cyclotomic-like; epsilon is a sign.
(iii) He sets up a direct check that phi_sigma is a homomorphism. Write f = (r s; t u), f' = (r' s'; t' u'), f'' = f(u'u), with mu'' = mu mu' and eps'' = eps eps' (15). The f-law of (12) becomes f'' = f' . u' f u'^{-1} (16), where u' now stands for phi_sigma(u').

The key explicit input is that phi_sigma(u) is reconstructed from the bottom row (t,u) of f and the scalars:
- phi_sigma(u) = mu . (u  eps t ; -t  eps u),
- with the norm relation t^2 + u^2 = eps/mu (next page),
- so det phi_sigma(u) = mu^2 . eps(t^2+u^2) = mu (the 'NB det u' = mu'').

The inverse is then simply the adjugate (eps u  -eps t ; t  u); the scalar factor mu'/mu' he wrote and struck out cancels. On the next page he expands the product. Using t'^2 + u'^2 = eps'/mu', the bottom row of f'' simplifies 'miraculously'. Rebuilding phi_sigma(u'u) from that bottom row gives phi_sigma(u') phi_sigma(u), i.e. the homomorphism property.

Purpose: show that the linearized ('abelianized') shadow of the action of this GT-like group is a genuine representation into GL(2,Z^), given explicitly by a norm-form parametrization. He remarks (next page) that this should be organized conceptually, e.g. via quaternions or norm forms, but he is too lazy ('la flemme') to do it.
errors: On the next page, formula (18) gives u'' = (1/mu')(-t t' + u u') while the displayed matrix has -eps' t t' + u u'. This is an eps' inconsistency (slip or transcription); the final verification uses yet another variant, so the signs need care.

On this page the explicit matrix product needs a scalar factor mu' on phi_sigma(u') and no extra factor on its inverse (the adjugate), since det phi_sigma(u') = mu'. The machine transcription's two factors 1/mu' are wrong. The manuscript shows a mu' and a struck-out mu'/mu'.

ideas.what: Linearization of the cocycle composition laws for automorphisms of Pi_{0,3}^ to GL(2,Z^); the profinite formulas are not explicit, the linear ones are
ideas.modern_name: Abelianized/linear quotient of the Grothendieck-Teichmüller action; cocycle (crossed homomorphism) formalism for GT
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1990s) for GT and its linear images
ideas.where_published: Longue Marche (1981) treats related questions; this specific computation unsure

ideas.what: Multiplicativity of the characters mu and epsilon_2 under composition
ideas.modern_name: Cyclotomic-type character and sign character on GT-like groups

ideas.what: Explicit parametrization phi(u) = mu (u eps t; -t eps u) with t^2+u^2 = eps/mu, recovered from the bottom row of f, and a direct check that phi is a homomorphism
ideas.modern_name: Norm-form (Gaussian-integer/quaternion-like) parametrization of a subgroup of GL(2,Z^)

missed.claim: Grothendieck notes the computation should fit into a conceptual linear-algebra framework (quaternions / norm forms describing the tilde M_{0,3} data (alpha, beta, f)) and leaves this undeveloped.
missed.quote: on sent que ces calculs devraient s'insérer dans un tapis d'algèbre linéaire que j'ai la flemme de dérouler in extenso
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. The linear image of GT-type actions on Pi^ab is well understood, so a conceptual repackaging would be expository rather than new.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine verification that an explicitly parametrized linear shadow of a GT-like action is a homomorphism. It is correct up to sign slips and contains nothing beyond standard linear algebra.
transcription_corrections: In the explicit product, the factor before (u' eps't'; -t' eps'u') is mu' (overwritten), not 1/mu'. The factor before (eps'u' -eps't'; t' u') is a struck mu'/mu', i.e. no factor, not 1/mu'.
The inserted data line reads 'f'', h', f'' with 'f'' crossed; the intended list is the data f, g, h of u and u'.
'quantités comme u'(g(u))' with an underbrace labelled g is correct; 'données ... = g(u) etc' refers to g' = g(u') etc.
